title: Overlapping Range Query Endpoint Bugs
pattern: Implementing range overlap checks by testing individual endpoints using complex compound inequalities with inclusive comparison operators (`<=`, `>=`) on exclusive endpoints.
why_bad: This pattern is structurally bug-prone. It miscalculates adjacent ranges (e.g. claiming `[0, 2)` overlaps with `[2, 4)` because of the `<=` check), and completely fails to detect cases where one range fully encloses the other without its endpoints falling inside.
detection: Look for range overlap functions using nested `&&` and `||` inequality checks on `begin`/`end` or `start`/`stop` fields.
source: *The Art of Readable Code* by Dustin Boswell and Trevor Foucher (Chapter 8, pp. 86-87).
